Class 2 · Chapter 1 of 9

Hundreds, tens and ones

Build, compare and say three-digit numbers like 342.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

By the end I can…

  • I can read hundreds, tens and ones.
  • I can order and compare numbers.
  • I can match a three-digit number to its written name.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 5

Ten tens make one hundred

Ten ones make a ten. Ten tens make a hundred.

Here is one hundred: 10 rows with 10 dots in each row.

Screen 2 of 5

Read a three-digit number

The number 342 has three digits.

3 is hundreds, 4 is tens and 2 is ones. So 342 is 3 hundreds, 4 tens and 2 ones.

Screen 3 of 5

A zero holds the place

In 305 there are 3 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones.

The zero says there are no tens. It keeps the 5 in the ones place.

Screen 4 of 5

Which number is bigger?

Compare the hundreds first. If they match, compare the tens, then the ones.

342 and 324 have 3 hundreds. 4 tens is more than 2 tens, so 342 is bigger.

Screen 5 of 5

Say the number name

Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

342 is said "three hundred and forty-two".

Words to know
hundred
Ten tens. A big group of 100.
digit
One of the symbols 0 to 9. Where a digit sits gives its value.
place value
The job a digit does: hundreds, tens or ones.

Chapter passed. Next: Add, subtract and make equal groups

For parents

What your child learns

In a 3-digit number, hundreds, tens and ones each have a value. A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a cube is 1. So 3 flats, 3 rods and 6 cubes make 336. Number clues narrow the choices.

A common slip

Children often read blocks in the wrong order, or forget a zero when a place is empty. Count the flats first, then rods, then cubes. Write 0 for a missing place.

5-minute home activity: Build 3-digit numbers

  1. Cut paper squares for 100, strips for 10 and small bits for 1.
  2. Build 124 and say how many of each.
  3. Write a number clue, such as digits add to 7.
  4. Ask someone to find numbers that fit your clue.
